abstract.en: Hear the same alarm ringing every weekday morning.
abstract.cn: 想象每个工作日早晨响起的同一个闹钟。

examples.en: She finds her office job mundane but reliable.
examples.cn: 她觉得坐办公室的工作乏味但稳定。

examples.en: The report is full of mundane details about the budget.
examples.cn: 这份报告满是预算方面平淡琐碎的细节。

examples.en: His speech was far from mundane and kept everyone laughing.
examples.cn: 他的演讲一点也不平淡，逗得大家直笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「满地」——满地都是天天要做的琐事，平凡又乏味；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mundus（世界）→ mundanus（属于世界的）→ 晚期拉丁语「尘世的」→ 古法语 mondain → 英语 mundane，核心义「尘世；世上的」。

sensesIntro.en: Mundane starts with the world itself, moves to the ordinary things of the world, and ends with the dullness that ordinariness brings.
sensesIntro.cn: mundane 从「尘世」讲起，转到世上的普通事物，最后落到「平凡带来的乏味」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old wooden door opening onto the same small daily chores.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇旧木门后，每天都是同样的琐碎家务。

branches.en: The earthly sense keeps the religious contrast.
branches.cn: 「尘世」这一义项保留了宗教层面的对比。

branches.en: The ordinary sense widens to daily work.
branches.cn: 「平凡」这一义项扩展到日常工作。

branches.en: The dull sense adds mild disappointment.
branches.cn: 「乏味」这一义项带上了一点失望。

branches.en: Earthly matters are by definition everyday matters.
branches.cn: 尘世之事按定义就是日常之事。

branches.en: Something ordinary soon feels boring when it never changes.
branches.cn: 一成不变的普通事物很快就会让人感到乏味。

intro.en: Mundane is built on the Latin noun for the world, with English mundanity, mundanely, and mundaneness around it.
intro.cn: mundane 建立在拉丁语表示「世界」的名词之上，周围有 mundanity、mundanely 与 mundaneness 等英语派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mundus means the world, and the adjective mundanus means belonging to the world.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mundus 意为世界，形容词 mundanus 意为「属于世界的」。

items.example: Mundus supplies the world image.
items.exampleCN: mundus 提供「世界」这一意象。

items.example: The suffix -anus turns mundus into mundanus.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -anus 把 mundus 变成 mundanus。

items.example: Mundanus is the direct parent form.
items.exampleCN: mundanus 是直接的母体形式。

items.example: Old French reshaped the ending of the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 古法语改变了拉丁形式的词尾。

items.example: Mundane keeps both the earthly and the dull senses.
items.exampleCN: mundane 同时保留「尘世」与「乏味」两种含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mundanely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 mundanely。

items.example: Mundanely describes a plain way of doing something.
items.exampleCN: mundanely 描述平淡的做法。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms mundanity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 mundanity。

items.example: Mundanity names the quality of the mundane.
items.exampleCN: mundanity 指 mundane 所具有的性质。

definition_zh: 市政的；市镇的；自治市政府的
definition_en: relating to the government or the affairs of a city or town
core_image: 市政厅前的公告牌，贴着垃圾清运与水管维修通知
scene: 街区路口贴出通知，说水管要整修，周一早上会停水。A notice on the corner announces that the municipal water supply will be shut off on Monday morning for repairs.
sceneCN: 这里 municipal 是「市政的」（第 1 个义项：与市镇政府及其公共设施有关的）；句意为街角贴出通知，市镇供水将于周一上午因维修而停水。

pos.zh: 市政的；市镇的；地方自治的

derivatives.zh: 由 municipal 加名词后缀 -ity 构成：自治市；市镇政府
由 municipal 加副词后缀 -ly 构成：以市政方式；由市镇办理地
由 municipal 加动词后缀 -ize 构成：使归市有；对……实行市营

senses.title: Relating to a town or city government
senses.definition: connected with the government or the public services of a city or town
senses.definitionCN: 与市镇或城市的地方政府或公共服务有关的
senses.example: The municipal library stays open until nine on weekdays.
senses.exampleCN: 市立图书馆工作日开放到晚上九点。
senses.why: Latin municipium named a town whose citizens held the rights of Roman citizens, so the adjective from it always points to the affairs of a self-governing town.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 municipium 指居民享有罗马公民权的自治城镇，由此而来的形容词自然总是指向自治市镇的事务。

senses.title: Of local rather than national authority
senses.titleCN: 地方性的；与中央相对的
senses.definition: belonging to the level of local administration below the national government
senses.definitionCN: 属于国家政府之下的地方行政层级
senses.example: Recycling is handled by municipal rather than national agencies.
senses.exampleCN: 回收工作由市镇机构而非国家机构负责。
senses.why: Because the town is the unit behind the word, it marks the step in government just above the neighbourhood and below the state.
senses.whyCN: 由于「城镇」是这个词背后的单位，它标示出高于街区、低于国家的行政层级。

senses.title: Owned or provided by a town
senses.definition: owned, run, or provided by a town for its residents
senses.definitionCN: 由市镇所有、经营或为居民提供
senses.example: The municipal swimming pool is free for children under twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 市营游泳池对十二岁以下儿童免费。
senses.why: Once a town owns and runs its services, the adjective shifts from the office to the things it operates.
senses.whyCN: 一旦市镇拥有并经营各项服务，该形容词就从「政府机构」延伸到「它所运营的设施」。

intro.en: Municipal goes back to Latin municipium, a town with its own laws whose leading men took on duties for Rome, from munus, a duty, and capere, to take.
intro.cn: municipal 源于拉丁语 municipium（有自己法律、其要员为罗马承担义务的城镇），由 munus（义务）与 capere（拿、承担）构成。

items.en: Munus means a duty, gift, or public charge.
items.cn: munus 意为义务、馈赠或公职。

items.en: Municipium names a self-governing town of Roman citizens that shared burdens with Rome.
items.cn: municipium 指与罗马分担义务、居民享有罗马公民权的自治城镇。

items.en: The adjective municipalis describes what belongs to such a town.
items.cn: 形容词 municipalis 描述属于此类城镇的事物。

items.en: The form passes into French municipal, used for the affairs of a town or commune.
items.cn: 该词形传入法语 municipal，用于指城镇或市镇的事务。

items.en: English municipal is attested in law for the internal affairs of a town.
items.cn: 英语 municipal 最早见于法律文本，指城镇的内部事务。

items.en: The word broadens with city governments, public utilities, and elections.
items.cn: 随着市政府、公共事业与选举的出现，词义也随之扩展。

note.en: Municipal belongs to the Latin family of munus and is close in meaning to civic and urban words.
note.cn: municipal 属于拉丁语 munus 一族，意义上与 civic、urban 一类词相邻。

entries.definition: a town or city with its own local government
entries.definitionCN: 自治市；市镇政府

entries.definition: a duty or public office, in Latin
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「义务、公职」，是这个词的词根

entries.definition: shared religious or emotional fellowship
entries.definitionCN: 共享的宗教或情感联结（同含 mun- 成分，词源分化较远）

entries.definition: relating to a city and the duties of its citizens
entries.definitionCN: 城市的；公民的

entries.definition: relating to a town or city as a place
entries.definitionCN: 城市的；都市的

entries.definition: relating to a particular nearby area
entries.definitionCN: 地方的；本地的

normalIntro.en: Municipal is the adjective of the town that shares burdens: munus is a duty, so municipal affairs are the town duties done for you.
normalIntro.cn: municipal 是「分担义务的城镇」的形容词：munus 是义务，所以市政事务就是替居民承担的那份职责。

normal.en: Municipal government is the town or city government.
normal.cn: municipal government 就是市镇政府。

normal.en: Municipal waste is household and business rubbish collected by the town.
normal.cn: municipal waste 是市镇统一清运的垃圾。

normal.en: Municipality is the noun for the town itself.
normal.cn: municipality 是表示「自治市」的名词。

normal.en: Compare civic: civic stresses citizens and their duties, municipal stresses the town as a unit of government.
normal.cn: 对比 civic：civic 强调市民与公民责任，municipal 强调作为行政单位的市镇。

normal.en: Latin munus gives municipal its duty sense and also underlies the English word remunerate.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 munus 给 municipal 带来「义务」之意，也构成英语 remunerate。

abstract.en: Picture a town hall clock with rubbish trucks parked below.
abstract.cn: 想象市政厅的大钟，楼下停着垃圾清运车。

abstract.en: See a public tap turning off at midday for repair.
abstract.cn: 想象正午时分公共水龙头因维修而关闭。

abstract.en: Imagine a form at the counter stamped with a town seal.
abstract.cn: 想象柜台上一张表格盖上了市镇公章。

examples.en: The municipal council voted to build a new bridge.
examples.cn: 市议会投票决定修建一座新桥。

examples.en: Municipal workers cleared the snow from the main roads.
examples.cn: 市政工人清除了主干道上的积雪。

examples.en: Most residents reuse the municipal bins each week.
examples.cn: 大多数居民每周都使用市镇的垃圾桶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谬你有车」——车停哪儿要问市政府，市政事务一本账；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 munus（义务、公职）+ capere（拿、承担）→ municipium（分担义务的自治城镇）→ municipalis → 英语 municipal，核心义「市镇承担的公职事务」。

sensesIntro.en: Municipal begins with the town government itself, moves to that level of authority, and ends with the services the town owns and runs.
sensesIntro.cn: municipal 先从市镇政府本身讲起，再指这一级行政层级，最后指市镇所有并运营的服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a notice board in front of the town hall.
core.cn: 核心意象：市政厅门前的那块公告牌。

branches.en: The town government sense is the source sense.
branches.cn: 市镇政府这一义项是源头义项。

branches.en: The local level sense names the rung of government.
branches.cn: 地方层级这一义项指政府架构中的一级。

branches.en: The publicly owned sense covers what the town runs.
branches.cn: 市有这一义项覆盖市镇运营的设施。

branches.en: A municipal body is a local body by definition.
branches.cn: 市政机构按定义就是地方机构。

branches.en: The town owns its pools and buses through the same government that issues the notices.
branches.cn: 市镇通过同一个政府既发布通知，也拥有游泳池与公交车。

intro.en: Municipal is built from the Latin duty noun munus and the verb capere, with English municipality, municipally, and municipalize around it.
intro.cn: municipal 由拉丁语表示「义务」的 munus 与动词 capere 构成，周围有 municipality、municipally 与 municipalize 等英语派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin municipium joins munus, a duty, with capere, to take, so the town is literally the place that takes on duties.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 municipium 把 munus（义务）与 capere（承担）结合起来，字面上就是「承担义务之地」。

items.meaning: a duty, gift, or public office
items.example: Munus gives the duty image.
items.exampleCN: munus 提供「义务」这一意象。

items.example: Capere contributes the taking of a burden.
items.exampleCN: capere 贡献「承担重担」之意。

items.example: Municipium is the compound source.
items.exampleCN: municipium 是复合来源词。

items.example: The suffix -alis forms municipalis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -alis 构成 municipalis。

items.example: Municipal keeps the town sense.
items.exampleCN: municipal 保留「城镇」含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或实体的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms municipality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 municipality。

items.meaning: a town with its own government
items.example: Municipality names the town as an entity.
items.exampleCN: municipality 把市镇指为一个实体。

items.example: Municipally funded means paid for by the town.
items.exampleCN: municipally funded 意为由市镇出资。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms municipalize.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ize 构成 municipalize。

definition_zh: 浑浊的；昏暗的；晦涩难懂的；可疑的
definition_en: dark and dirty in a way that you cannot see through, hard to understand, or morally doubtful
core_image: 一场暴雨后，池塘里翻起泥浆，看不清水底
scene: 早上从店里买来的水看起来发浑，放一会儿就沉下一层泥沙。The water from the tap looked murky for a few minutes after the pipe repair.
sceneCN: 这里 murky 是「浑浊的」（第 1 个义项：因有杂质而看不清的）；句意为修完水管后的几分钟里，水龙头流出的水看起来发浑。

derivatives.zh: 由 murky 剥离词尾得来的名词：黑暗；昏暗（也可作形容词用）
由 murky 的 y 改 i 加副词后缀 -ly 构成：浑浊地；晦涩地
由 murky 的 y 改 i 加名词后缀 -ness 构成：浑浊；晦涩；可疑

senses.title: Dark and not clear enough to see through
senses.definition: dark and full of dirt or other material so that you cannot see through it
senses.definitionCN: 昏暗且含泥沙或其他杂质，因而看不清
senses.example: Divers could not see the end of the tunnel in the murky water.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在浑浊的水中看不到隧道的尽头。
senses.why: Old English mirce meant dark, and the noun murk was the darkness itself, so murky first describes anything that hides its bottom in shadow or dirt.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mirce 意为昏暗，名词 murk 就是「黑暗」本身；因此 murky 首先形容把底细藏在阴影或污浊里的东西。

senses.title: Cloudy and gloomy in the air
senses.definition: grey and gloomy, as if covered in haze or smoke
senses.definitionCN: 灰蒙蒙、阴沉沉的，像被雾气或烟罩住
senses.example: The town lay under a murky sky for most of the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个冬天大部分时间，小镇都笼罩在阴沉的天色下。
senses.why: Darkness also lives in the air itself, so the same word stretches from dirty water to a sky that refuses to brighten.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗也存在于空气中，于是这个词从污浊的水扩展到始终亮不起来的天色。

senses.title: Hard to understand
senses.definition: unclear and difficult to understand because it is vague or complicated
senses.definitionCN: 表达不清、因含糊或复杂而难以理解
senses.example: The contract is full of murky clauses about who pays for damage.
senses.exampleCN: 合同里关于谁来支付损坏赔偿的条款写得含糊不清。
senses.why: What you cannot see through in water becomes what you cannot see through with the mind, so unclear wording is murky too.
senses.whyCN: 水里看不清的东西，换成头脑也看不清，就成了晦涩的表达。

senses.title: Suspicious and not completely honest
senses.definition: unclear in a way that suggests something dishonest or secret is going on
senses.definitionCN: 不清楚得让人怀疑有不当或秘密的事
senses.example: The bank withdrew from a project with murky finances.
senses.exampleCN: 银行退出了那个财务不明不白的项目。
senses.why: Anything kept in the dark is easy to suspect, so murky moves from the literal dark to dealings that do not want to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 藏在暗处的东西容易被怀疑，于是 murky 从字面的「暗」引申到「不想被看见」的交易。

intro.en: Murky joins Old English mirce, dark, and murc, darkness, into an adjective, with the base noun murk rebuilt in later English.
intro.cn: murky 把古英语 mirce（昏暗）与 murc（黑暗）合为形容词，后世的英语又回构出名名词 murk。

items.en: A reconstructed form along the lines of mirkwja is generally assumed for dark in the older Germanic languages.
items.cn: 一般认为，日耳曼语较早时期有一个意为「昏暗」的重构形式（约作 mirkwja）。

items.en: Mirce means dark or obscure, and murc is the darkness itself.
items.cn: mirce 意为昏暗、阴暗，murc 指黑暗本身。

items.en: The adjective appears as mirke or murke, with the dark sense intact.
items.cn: 该形容词写作 mirke 或 murke，保持昏暗之意。

items.en: Murk is rebuilt as the noun behind murky and later spreads to foggy weather.
items.cn: murk 被回构为 murky 背后的名词，后来又用于雾蒙蒙的天气。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth century writing extends murky to unclear ideas and shady money.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪的文字把 murky 扩展到模糊的观点与见不得光的金钱。

note.en: Murky is the adjective of darkness and muddiness, close in form to murk and murkiness and in meaning to cloudy and shady words.
note.cn: murky 是表示「昏暗、浑浊」的形容词，形式上与 murk、murkiness 同族，意义上与 cloudy、shady 一类词相邻。

entries.definition: darkness or heavy mist
entries.definitionCN: 黑暗；浓雾

entries.definition: the state of being murky
entries.definitionCN: 浑浊；晦涩的状态

entries.definition: kindness shown to someone in a bad position
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈；宽恕（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: full of cloud, or not clear
entries.definitionCN: 多云的；混浊的

entries.definition: protected from the sun, or of doubtful honesty
entries.definitionCN: 背阴的；可疑的

entries.definition: not expressed or understood clearly
entries.definitionCN: 含糊的；模糊的

normalIntro.en: Murky starts from mirce, the old word for dark, and keeps the picture of something you cannot see through.
normalIntro.cn: murky 源自表示「昏暗」的古词 mirce，始终保留「看不透里面」的画面。

normal.en: Murky water is so dirty you cannot see the bottom.
normal.cn: murky water 就是脏得看不见水底的水。

normal.en: Murk is the noun of darkness behind the adjective.
normal.cn: murk 是形容词背后的「黑暗」名词。

normal.en: A murky past is a history with parts the person would rather hide.
normal.cn: murky past 指有部分不愿示人的过去。

normal.en: Murky dealings are negotiations that look dishonest.
normal.cn: murky dealings 指看起来不诚实的交易。

normal.en: Compare shady: shady suggests secrecy, murky that the dishonesty is hard to pin down.
normal.cn: 对比 shady：shady 强调偷偷摸摸，murky 强调不当之处难以查清。

abstract.en: Stir the bottom of a pond and watch the mud rise.
abstract.cn: 想象搅动池塘底部，泥沙翻上来。

abstract.en: Look at a window in fog and see only grey.
abstract.cn: 想象雾天隔着窗户，只看见一片灰。

abstract.en: Skim a page of tiny grey lines that refuses to make sense.
abstract.cn: 想象扫一眼满是灰色小字的页面，却读不出意思。

examples.en: The pond was murky after the heavy rain.
examples.cn: 大雨过后，池塘变得浑浊。

examples.en: No one understood the murky rules about overtime pay.
examples.cn: 没人能弄懂关于加班费那些含糊不清的规定。

examples.en: Investigators traced the money through several murky accounts.
examples.cn: 调查人员顺着数个可疑账户追查这笔钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸黑」——在浑水里摸黑看不见底，事情也说不清；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 mirce（昏暗）、murc（黑暗），一般认为可上溯到日耳曼语重构形式 mirkwja → 中古英语 mirke → 英语 murky，核心义「看不透的暗」。

sensesIntro.en: Murky begins with dark and dirty water, spreads to a gloomy sky, then to words that hide their meaning, and finally to dealings that hide their honesty.
sensesIntro.cn: murky 从昏暗污浊的水讲起，扩到阴沉的天色，再到藏住含义的措辞，最后到藏住诚信的交易。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pond churned to mud after the rain, bottom invisible.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后翻起泥浆、看不见底的池塘。

branches.en: The dirty water sense is the literal core.
branches.cn: 浑浊的水是字面上的核心义项。

branches.en: The gloomy air sense moves darkness into the sky.
branches.cn: 阴沉天色这一义项把黑暗移到天空。

branches.en: The unclear meaning sense moves darkness into language.
branches.cn: 含义不明这一义项把黑暗移到语言里。

branches.en: A vague clause often shelters a hidden motive.
branches.cn: 含糊的条款里往往藏着隐秘动机。

branches.en: Dirty water and dirty money share the same image of mud.
branches.cn: 污浊的水与见不得光的钱共享「泥」的意象。

intro.en: Murky is an English adjective built on the old Germanic root for dark, with murk, murkily, and murkiness around it.
intro.cn: murky 是建立在古日耳曼语表示「昏暗」的词根之上的英语形容词，周围有 murk、murkily 与 murkiness 等词。

latinIntro.en: Murky has no Latin ancestor; its base is the Old English mirce and murc, so the Latin layer here is empty.
latinIntro.cn: murky 没有拉丁语祖先，其底子是古英语 mirce 与 murc，因此这一层的拉丁同源词为空。

items.example: Mirce gives the dark image.
items.exampleCN: mirce 提供「昏暗」这一意象。

items.example: Murc names the darkness itself.
items.exampleCN: murc 指黑暗本身。

items.example: Mirk is the Middle English shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: mirk 是该词的中古英语形式。

items.example: Murk is the reclaimed noun.
items.exampleCN: murk 是后来回构出的名词。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y turns murk into murky.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 murk 变成 murky。

items.example: Murky carries all three shades.
items.exampleCN: murky 兼具三种引申义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms murkily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 murkily。

items.meaning: in a dark or unclear way
items.example: Murkily describes a dim way of seeing or writing.
items.exampleCN: murkily 描述看不清楚或写得含糊的方式。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms murkiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 murkiness。

definition_zh: 沉思；冥想；缪斯女神；灵感；诗人
definition_en: to think about something carefully and quietly; also a spirit said to inspire art, or such inspiration itself
core_image: 一个人站在窗前出神，眼睛望着远处，嘴唇微动像在对自己念叨
scene: 写完最后一段文章，她放下笔，望着窗外的雨发了很久的呆。She put down her pen and mused on what her title really meant.
sceneCN: 这里 muse 是「沉思」（第 1 个义项：安静而深入地想事情）；句意：她放下笔，思索自己的标题究竟是什么意思。

pos.zh: 沉思；冥想；若有所思地说

collocations.zh: （沉思）思考某事；在心里反复琢磨
缪斯九女神（掌管文艺的众神）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「沉思；冥想」，也作形容词「若有所思的」
由前缀 be- 与 muse 的「发呆」义构成，义为「使困惑、使茫然」，并派生形容词 bemused
一般认为由前缀 be- 与 muse 的「发呆」义结合，义为「困惑的；茫然的」

senses.title: To think quietly and deeply
senses.definition: to think about something in a quiet, dreamy, unhurried way
senses.definitionCN: 安静、出神、不慌不忙地思考某事
senses.example: She mused on the old letter for a long while.
senses.exampleCN: 她对着那封旧信沉思了很久。
senses.why: The core image is a person lost in reverie, so the verb names quiet unworldly thinking.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一个人出神凝想，所以动词指安静、不触及现实的思考。

senses.title: To say something thoughtfully
senses.definition: to say something slowly and reflectively, often to yourself
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而带着思索地说出某话，常是自言自语
senses.example: He mused aloud, wondering why the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他自言自语地想着计划为何失败。
senses.why: Thinking aloud turns the silent reflection into half-spoken words.
senses.whyCN: 把心里想的说出来，安静的沉思就变成半出声的话语。

senses.title: A goddess of the arts
senses.definition: any of the nine Greek goddesses who were said to inspire poetry, music, and learning
senses.definitionCN: 希腊神话中掌管诗歌、音乐与学问的九位启发灵感的女儿
senses.example: The poet asked the Muse for a worthy subject.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人向缪斯女神祈求一个配得上的题材。
senses.why: The noun sense comes straight from the Greek myth: the goddess who breathes inspiration into the artist.
senses.whyCN: 名词义直接来自希腊神话：女神把灵感吹进艺术家的心里。

senses.title: Inspiration for creation
senses.definition: a source of artistic inspiration or the spirit that moves someone to create
senses.definitionCN: 艺术灵感的来源，或促使人创作的那种精神
senses.example: The river valley was the painter s constant muse.
senses.exampleCN: 那片河谷是这位画家不竭的灵感来源。
senses.why: Once a goddess can inspire, the inspiring force itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 既然女神能给人灵感，那股启发人创作的力量本身也就得了这个名字。

senses.title: A state of contemplation
senses.definition: a spell of absorbed reflection, often shown by an absent look
senses.definitionCN: 一段沉浸在思索中的时光，常表现为心不在焉的神情
senses.example: He sank into a muse at the sound of the bell.
senses.exampleCN: 听到钟声他陷入一种凝想出神的状态。
senses.why: The act of musing shades into the mood or spell of being lost in thought.
senses.whyCN: 沉思这个动作会延伸成一整段走神出神的心境。

intro.en: Muse comes through French and Latin from Greek Mousa, one of the nine divine sisters of song and memory, and its verb form musein, to sing or to think deeply.
intro.cn: muse 经法语和拉丁语来自希腊语 mousa（缪斯，掌管诗歌与记忆的九位女神之一），其动词形式 musein 意为歌唱或深思。

items.en: Mousa names one of the nine goddesses of song and memory.
items.cn: 希腊语 mousa 指掌管歌唱与记忆的九位女神之一。

items.en: The verb musein means to sing or to consider in silence.
items.cn: 动词 musein 意为歌唱或默然思索。

items.en: Musa keeps both the goddess and the act of song.
items.cn: 拉丁语 musa 保留了女神之名与歌唱之事。

items.en: The verb muser means to pause, dally, or dream.
items.cn: 古法语动词 muser 意为逗留、闲荡或发呆。

items.en: Muse enters English for thinking with the mind elsewhere.
items.cn: muse 进入中古英语，指心不在焉地思考。

items.en: The noun keeps the goddess sense, while the verb settles on deep thought.
items.cn: 现代英语名词保留女神义，动词则稳定在「深思」义上。

note.en: Muse is the thinking verb rooted in the Greek Muses, alongside the adjective bemused and ordinary thinking words.
note.cn: muse 是以希腊缪斯女神为词根的「思考」动词，旁边有形容词 bemused 以及普通的「思考」类词。

entries.definition: a quiet spell of thought
entries.definitionCN: 沉思；冥想（muse 加 -ing 的名词形式）

entries.definition: puzzled or absorbed in thought
entries.definitionCN: 困惑的；茫然的，一般认为由 be- 加 muse 构成

entries.definition: a place devoted to the Muses and to the arts
entries.definitionCN: 博物馆；与缪斯同源，原指供缪斯女神的神殿

entries.definition: to think about something carefully for a long time
entries.definitionCN: 仔细而长久地思考

entries.definition: to think seriously and quietly about something
entries.definitionCN: 深思；反省

entries.definition: to think in a worried, unhappy way
entries.definitionCN: 忧思；焦虑地反复想

normalIntro.en: Muse joins the divine Muses with the small everyday act of thinking things over.
normalIntro.cn: muse 一端连着神圣的缪斯女神，一端连着日常的「把事情想上一遍」。

normal.en: To muse on something is to turn it over slowly in the mind.
normal.cn: muse on 某事就是把它在心里慢慢翻来覆去地想。

normal.en: Muse over a problem before you answer.
normal.cn: 回答问题前先 muse over 一番那个难题。

normal.en: The Muses are the nine Greek sisters who inspire song and poetry.
normal.cn: the Muses 就是启发诗歌与音乐的九位希腊女神。

normal.en: Museum shares its root: it was once a temple of the Muses.
normal.cn: museum 与它同根：最初就是缪斯女神的神殿。

normal.en: Compare ponder: ponder is deliberate and logical, muse is dreamy and poetic.
normal.cn: 对比 ponder：ponder 更审慎、讲逻辑，muse 更出神、更有诗意。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing at a window, eyes on the rain, lips moving quietly.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在窗前看雨，嘴唇轻轻动着。

abstract.en: Imagine whispering your thought aloud to yourself at your desk.
abstract.cn: 想象你坐在桌前，把心里的念头小声念给自己听。

abstract.en: See nine sisters handing a poet a quill made of light.
abstract.cn: 想象九位姐妹把一支发光的羽毛笔递给诗人。

examples.en: She mused on the strange outcome of the match.
examples.cn: 她沉思着那场比赛古怪的结果。

examples.en: The old teacher mused aloud about the passing years.
examples.cn: 老教师若有所思地念叨着逝去的岁月。

examples.en: Some poets still invoke the Muse before they begin.
examples.cn: 一些诗人动笔前仍会呼唤缪斯女神。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缪斯」——文艺女神的名字，出神想着她，就是沉思；这只是谐音联想，与词源解释不同。

root: 希腊语 mousa（缪斯女神，掌管诗歌与记忆）→ musein（歌唱；沉思）→ 拉丁语 musa → 古法语 muser（发呆、闲荡）→ 英语 muse，核心义「受灵感而动、出神深思」。

sensesIntro.en: Muse moves from the quiet inner act of thinking, to speaking half aloud, back to the inspiring goddess, and finally to the inspiration and the mood itself.
sensesIntro.cn: muse 先从安静的内心思考出发，延伸到半出声的念叨，再回到启发创作的缪斯女神，最后落在灵感与出神的心境本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing by a window, lost in quiet thought.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在窗前，安静地出神。

branches.en: Quiet thinking is the everyday verb sense.
branches.cn: 安静思考是动词的日常义项。

branches.en: Thinking aloud turns reflection into speech.
branches.cn: 出声思索把内省变成了话语。

branches.en: The Greek goddess sense is the mythic source.
branches.cn: 希腊女神义是神话源头。

branches.en: Inspiration and the absorbing mood both grow from the goddess.
branches.cn: 灵感义与沉醉心境都从女神形象生长出来。

branches.en: Reflection and musing aloud share one slow rhythm of thought.
branches.cn: 独思与念叨共享同一种缓慢的思维节奏。

intro.en: Muse has no separable prefix or suffix of its own; English builds around it with -ing, be-, and the related museum and music.
intro.cn: muse 本身没有可拆的前缀或后缀，英语围绕它构成 -ing 形式、be- 形式，以及同族的 museum 与 music。

latinIntro.en: Latin took Musa from Greek, keeping both a goddess and an act of song; the verb sense of musing grew in French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借来 musa，同时保留女神之名与歌唱之事；「沉思」的动词义则在法语中长成。

items.meaning: a Muse, a goddess of song
items.example: Mousa is the oldest form of the goddess name.
items.exampleCN: mousa 是女神名最古老的形式。

items.example: Latin musa carries the goddess into Europe.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 musa 把女神带进了欧洲。

items.example: The suffix -ing makes musing from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 由动词构成 musing。

items.meaningCN: 表示「彻底地、使处于某状态」
items.example: The prefix be- helps form bemused.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 be- 帮助构成 bemused。

items.meaning: a building that keeps art and objects
items.example: Museum literally meant a seat of the Muses.
items.exampleCN: museum 字面意思是缪斯的居所。

items.example: Music takes its name from the same goddesses.
items.exampleCN: music（音乐）同样得名于这几位女神。

items.example: Musical follows music into the adjective.
items.exampleCN: musical 由 music 派生为形容词。

items.example: The phrase muse on is the most common use.
items.exampleCN: muse on 是最常见的搭配。

items.example: Musing can also work as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: musing 也可作形容词用。

latinEntries.meaning: music, the art of the Muses

definition_zh: 芥末；芥菜；芥末黄；强烈的趣味
definition_en: a hot yellow paste made from crushed mustard seeds; also the plant that gives these seeds, and the yellow colour of the paste
core_image: 一勺鲜黄的芥末酱，入口先不发辣，过一会儿辣味直冲鼻子
scene: 三明治太干了，她在面包上抹了薄薄一层黄酱，咬下去顿时冲鼻。A thin layer of mustard made the plain sandwich taste sharp and warm.
sceneCN: 这里 mustard 是「芥末」（第 1 个义项：用芥菜籽磨成的辛辣黄色酱料）；句意：薄薄一层芥末让普通三明治变得辛辣而温热。

collocations.zh: 第戎芥末（法国第戎出产的淡黄芥末酱）
一粒芥籽（比喻微小却有力的开端）

derivatives.zh: 由 mustard 加 -y 构成，义为「有芥末味的；像芥末的」
mustard 与 seed 组成的复合词，义为「芥菜籽」，也用于比喻极小的开端

senses.title: The hot yellow paste
senses.definition: a sharp yellow paste made from crushed mustard seeds and served with food
senses.definitionCN: 用磨碎的芥菜籽加调料制成的辛辣黄色酱料，佐餐食用
senses.example: He added a spoonful of mustard to the hot dog.
senses.exampleCN: 他往热狗上加了一勺芥末酱。
senses.why: The prepared condiment is the most familiar meaning, because the plant became food only after its seeds were crushed.
senses.whyCN: 调好的酱料是最熟悉的含义，因为芥菜只有把籽磨碎之后才真正成为食物。

senses.title: The plant and its seeds
senses.definition: a fast growing plant of the cabbage family, or its small round seeds
senses.definitionCN: 十字花科中生长很快的一种植物，或它结出的细小圆粒种子
senses.example: Farmers sow mustard as a cover crop between seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在季节之间播种芥菜作为覆盖作物。
senses.why: Before there was paste there was a plant, so the plant and seed keep the same name.
senses.whyCN: 在出现酱料之前先有植物，所以植物和种子沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: The colour of mustard
senses.definition: a brownish yellow colour like the prepared paste
senses.definitionCN: 像调好的芥末酱那样偏褐的黄色
senses.example: She wore a mustard scarf against the grey coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她在灰色大衣外系了一条芥末黄的围巾。
senses.why: The bright paste gave its colour a name in fashion and painting.
senses.whyCN: 鲜亮的芥末酱把自己的颜色带进了时尚与绘画的命名。

senses.title: Something that cuts the mustard
senses.definition: used in informal sayings to mean the quality that makes something good enough
senses.definitionCN: 用于口语说法，指使某事物合格、够用的那种品质
senses.example: This old printer still cuts the mustard for short letters.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧打印机对付短书信还算够用。
senses.why: Sharp mustard was prized for its bite, so the condiment came to stand for what is up to standard.
senses.whyCN: 辛辣的芥末因够劲味而受人看重，这味调料于是用来指「够标准的东西」。

senses.title: The pungent interest of a thing
senses.definition: the quality of being sharp and interesting, able to flavour something dull
senses.definitionCN: 使原本平淡之事有了刺激与趣味的那种辛辣锋芒
senses.example: Her dry wit was the mustard in an otherwise heavy meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 在沉闷的会议上，她那种不动声色的机锋是唯一的辛辣调味。
senses.why: The hot taste of mustard extends metaphorically to anything that gives life a sharp edge.
senses.whyCN: 芥末的辣味被引申为一切能让人生变锋利的刺激。

senses.title: The seed of a tiny beginning
senses.definition: a very small thing that is said to grow into something great
senses.definitionCN: 被说成能长成巨大事物的极小之物
senses.example: Their first two clients were the mustard seed of the company.
senses.exampleCN: 最早的两个客户就是这家公司的那粒芥籽。
senses.why: The Bible compares faith to a mustard seed, and the tiny seed image now stands for humble beginnings.
senses.whyCN: 《圣经》把信仰比作一粒芥籽，于是这一颗小小的种子成了微小开端的象征。

intro.en: Mustard came into English through Old French moustarde, from Latin mustum, the must or new wine that the crushed seeds were once mixed with.
intro.cn: mustard 经古法语 moustarde 进入英语，而该词来自拉丁语 mustum，即曾经用来拌磨碎芥末籽的葡萄汁（must）。

items.en: Mustum means must, the newly pressed juice of grapes.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mustum 意为葡萄汁、新酒。

items.en: Mustum ardens, burning must, names the hot paste.
items.cn: 拉丁语短语「灼热的葡萄汁」用来指这种辣酱。

items.en: Moustarde condenses the phrase into one word.
items.cn: 古法语 moustarde 把这一短语压缩成一个词。

items.en: English spellings shift from mustarde toward mustard.
items.cn: 英语拼写从 mustarde 逐渐变为 mustard。

items.en: Mustard appears in English recipes and herbals.
items.cn: mustard 在英语食谱与本草书中出现。

items.en: The word adds the plant, the colour, and the saying cut the mustard.
items.cn: 现代英语加上植物、颜色与「够格」习语等义项。

note.en: Mustard belongs to the mustard family and to the naming of sharp seasonings, close to related condiments and to words built on must.
note.cn: mustard 属于十字花科，也属于辛辣调味品的命名系统，与同类调料以及由 must 构成的词相邻。

entries.definition: to gather troops or support
entries.definitionCN: 集合；召集。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: tasting or looking like mustard
entries.definitionCN: 有芥末味的；像芥末的

entries.definition: the seed of the mustard plant
entries.definitionCN: 芥菜籽，也喻指微小却有力量的开始

entries.definition: a thick sweet sauce made from tomatoes
entries.definitionCN: 番茄酱（同类调味酱）

entries.definition: a very hot root sauce served with meat
entries.definitionCN: 辣根酱（与芥末同类的辛辣调料）

entries.definition: a hot green paste eaten with Japanese food
entries.definitionCN: 山葵酱（日本料理中辛辣的绿色蘸酱）

normalIntro.en: Mustard joins the Latin word for new wine with an English family of plant, seed, colour, and sharp-tasting words.
normalIntro.cn: mustard 一端连着拉丁语里表示新酒的词，一端连着英语中植物、种子、颜色与辛辣味构成的一族词。

normal.en: Mustard was once mixed with must, so the Latin word for grape juice is still inside it.
normal.cn: 芥末过去是和 must（葡萄汁）拌在一起的，所以葡萄汁的拉丁词仍藏在里面。

normal.en: The mustard plant, its seeds, and the paste share one name.
normal.cn: 芥菜、芥籽与芥末酱共用一个词。

normal.en: A mustard seed is the classic image of a tiny start.
normal.cn: 一粒芥籽是「微小开端」的经典比喻。

normal.en: To cut the mustard means to be good enough.
normal.cn: cut the mustard 就是达到要求、够格。

normal.en: Compare ketchup: ketchup is sweet and mild, mustard is sharp and hot.
normal.cn: 对比 ketchup：番茄酱甜而温和，芥末辛辣冲鼻。

abstract.en: Picture a spoonful of bright yellow paste beside a grey sandwich.
abstract.cn: 想象灰扑扑的三明治旁边摆着一勺明黄色的酱。

abstract.en: Feel the hot taste rise into your nose a second after you bite.
abstract.cn: 感受咬下去一秒之后辣味冲上鼻子的那股劲儿。

abstract.en: See one tiny round seed that grows into a whole field of yellow flowers.
abstract.cn: 看一粒小小的圆籽长成整片金黄的油菜花。

examples.en: Add a little mustard to balance the sweetness of the sauce.
examples.cn: 加一点芥末来平衡酱汁的甜味。

examples.en: The chef grinds mustard seeds fresh for each dish.
examples.cn: 这位厨师每道菜都现磨芥菜籽。

examples.en: His early sketches were the mustard seed of a long career.
examples.cn: 他早期的草图是他漫长职业生涯的那粒芥籽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「骂死它」——芥末辣得人一跳，仿佛在心里埋怨它；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mustum（新葡萄汁）→ 短语 mustum ardens（灼热的葡萄汁）→ 古法语 moustarde → 中古英语 mustarde → 现代英语 mustard，核心义「用搀了新酒的芥籽做成的辣酱」，再由植物、颜色、辛辣感扩展出比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: Mustard starts as a yellow paste, then names the plant and seed behind it, its colour, its idiomatic standard of quality, and finally any sharp flavour or tiny beginning.
sensesIntro.cn: mustard 从黄色酱料出发，先后指它背后的植物与种子、它的颜色、习语中的「合格」标准，最后延伸到任何辛辣趣味与微小开端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright yellow spoonful of sharp paste on a plain sandwich.
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺鲜黄的辛辣酱料放在平淡的三明治上。

branches.en: The prepared paste is the food sense.
branches.cn: 调好的酱料是食物义项。

branches.en: Plant and seed keep the original name.
branches.cn: 植物与种子沿用最初的名字。

branches.en: The paste lends its yellow to colour names.
branches.cn: 酱料的黄色被借作颜色名。

branches.en: The sharpness of taste becomes a metaphor for quality and interest.
branches.cn: 味道的锋利被引申为品质与趣味。

branches.en: The seed behind the paste gives the image of a tiny beginning.
branches.cn: 酱料背后的种子提供了微小开端的意象。

intro.en: Mustard has no productive prefix or suffix, but its mustard family and -seed compounds show how English extends a word for a condiment.
intro.cn: mustard 没有能产的前缀或后缀，但同族的 must 与 -seed 复合词显示了英语如何扩展一个调料名。

latinIntro.en: Latin mustum, the must of grapes, is the direct source of the first half of mustard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mustum（葡萄汁）是 mustard 前半部分的直接来源。

items.example: Mustum once described the fresh juice of grapes.
items.exampleCN: mustum 原指新榨的葡萄汁。

items.example: Ardens describes the heat a paste would give.
items.exampleCN: ardens 描述这种酱料带来的辣意。

items.example: Moustarde is the direct middle step.
items.exampleCN: moustarde 是直接的中介形式。

items.example: The suffix -y forms mustardy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 mustardy。

items.example: The compound mustardseed uses this ending.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 mustardseed 用了这个结尾。

items.example: Mustard covers both the sauce and the crop.
items.exampleCN: mustard 兼指酱料与作物。

items.example: Mustardy describes a sharp taste.
items.exampleCN: mustardy 描述辛辣滋味。

items.example: Mus may share a deep root with Latin mustum.
items.exampleCN: mus 可能与拉丁语 mustum 共享更深的词根。

items.meaning: the seed of the mustard plant
items.example: Mustardseed is used in proverbs.
items.exampleCN: mustardseed 常用于谚语。

definition_zh: 沉默的；不说话的；无声的；哑的；减弱音量的
definition_en: not speaking or making a sound, either by choice or because speech is impossible
core_image: 一个张开嘴却发不出声的人，嘴唇在动，空气却是静止的
scene: 屏幕上的小喇叭图标被点成一道斜线，整段视频顿时只剩画面。She pressed the button and the phone went mute for the whole meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 mute 是「静音的；不发声的」（第 3 个义项：设备被设为不发出声音）；句意：她按下按钮，整场会议手机都处于静音状态。

collocations.zh: 聋哑的（旧式说法，今多改用别的表述）

derivatives.zh: 由 mute 加 -ly 构成，义为「无声地；沉默不语地」
由 mute 加 -ness 构成，义为「沉默；无声；失语状态」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「（声音）低沉的；柔和的；（颜色）淡雅的」

senses.title: Choosing not to speak
senses.definition: staying silent on purpose, refusing to say anything
senses.definitionCN: 有意保持沉默，不愿说出任何话
senses.example: The minister stayed mute when asked about the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 被问到延误一事时，部长一言不发。
senses.why: The core image is a mouth with no sound leaving it, so the first sense is deliberate silence.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一张嘴却发不出声音，于是第一个义项便是有意的沉默。

senses.title: Unable to speak
senses.definition: physically unable to make sounds with the voice
senses.definitionCN: 生理上不能发声
senses.example: He was mute for a month after the operation on his throat.
senses.exampleCN: 喉咙手术之后他有一个月说不出话。
senses.why: From chosen silence the word comes to describe the impossibility of speech itself.
senses.whyCN: 从选择沉默，这个词转而描述说话本身的不可能。

senses.title: Set to make no sound
senses.definition: switched so that a device gives out no sound
senses.definitionCN: 把设备设置成不发出声音的状态
senses.example: The television was mute all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 整晚电视都是静音状态。
senses.why: A silent person and a silent machine look alike from outside, so the word moved onto controls and screens.
senses.whyCN: 沉默的人和不出声的机器在外表上一模一样，于是 mute 被用到了开关与屏幕上。

senses.title: Softened in sound
senses.definition: made less loud or less sharp, as of a horn or a sound
senses.definitionCN: 被减弱了音量或尖锐度，如号角或声音
senses.example: The car went past with a mute horn and dim lights.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆车鸣着闷哑的喇叭、亮着昏暗的灯过去了。
senses.why: The noun mute as a silencer on a horn leads to the idea of anything dulled in tone.
senses.whyCN: 名词 mute 指号角上的消音器，由此引申为任何音色被削弱的东西。

senses.title: Pale and subdued in colour
senses.definition: described of colour or tone that is soft rather than bright
senses.definitionCN: 形容颜色或色调柔和而不鲜亮
senses.example: The room was done in mute greens and warm greys.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间用的是柔和的绿色与温暖的灰色。
senses.why: Quiet sound and quiet colour share the same idea of lowered intensity.
senses.whyCN: 安静的声音和安静的颜色共享同一个「降低强度」的概念。

senses.title: A device that silences
senses.definition: an object or control used to deaden sound
senses.definitionCN: 用来压低声音的物件或按键
senses.example: The trumpet player fitted a mute before the gentle passage.
senses.exampleCN: 小号手在那段轻柔乐句前装上了弱音器。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a countable noun for the very thing that makes something mute.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化成可数名词，专指让某物变得安静的那个东西。

senses.title: Silent in a figurative way
senses.definition: said of things, evidence, or places that say nothing yet tell a story
senses.definitionCN: 形容事物、证据或地方虽不言语却在说明事情
senses.example: The empty table was a mute witness to the quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 那张空桌子是那场争吵无声的见证者。
senses.why: Once silence can be chosen, anything wordless can be called mute.
senses.whyCN: 既然沉默可以是一种选择，任何无言之物都能被称为 mute。

intro.en: Mute comes from Latin mutus, without speech, which passed through Old French muet into English; it is related to mutter and murmur.
intro.cn: mute 来自拉丁语 mutus（不说话的），经古法语 muet 进入英语；它与 mutter、murmur（低声嘟囔）有亲缘关系。

items.en: A reconstructed root mut- is generally linked to sounds made with closed lips.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 mut-，与闭唇发出的声音有关。

items.en: Mutus means silent or unable to speak.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutus 意为沉默的、不能说话的。

items.en: Mutus also names a person without speech.
items.cn: mutus 也可用作名词，指不会说话的人。

items.en: Muet softens the Latin ending in French.
items.cn: 古法语 muet 缓和了拉丁语的词尾。

items.en: Mute appears in English for a person without speech.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪用 mute 指不能说的人。

items.en: Mute spreads to machines, colours, and music.
items.cn: 现代英语把 mute 扩展到机器、颜色与音乐上。

note.en: Mute is the Latin word for speechlessness, next to a family of mutter, murmur, and mutual and to everyday words for silence.
note.cn: mute 是拉丁语中表示「不能说话」的词，旁边有 mutter、murmur、mutual 等形近词，以及日常的「安静」类词。

entries.definition: softened in sound or colour
entries.definitionCN: 声音或色彩柔和的；压抑的

entries.definition: to speak in a low, unclear voice
entries.definitionCN: 低声嘟囔；低语

entries.definition: the common European swan, so called for its quiet call
entries.definitionCN: 疣鼻天鹅，因叫声低沉而得名

entries.definition: making no sound at all
entries.definitionCN: 无声的；安静的

entries.definition: unable to speak, often from shock
entries.definitionCN: 说不出话的；语塞的

entries.definition: having no voice, or having no say
entries.definitionCN: 失声的；（比喻）没有发言权的

normalIntro.en: Mute sits in a Latin family of quiet sounds: mutus without speech, mutter, and murmur.
normalIntro.cn: mute 处在一个表示安静声音的拉丁语族里：mutus（无声）、mutter（嘟囔）、murmur（低语）。

normal.en: Latin mutus means unable to speak, so a mute person has no words.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mutus 意为不能说话，所以 mute 的人是没话可说的。

normal.en: Mutter and murmur share the closed-lip sound that mute carries.
normal.cn: mutter 与 murmur 都共享 mute 所含的闭唇声音。

normal.en: The mute button is the everyday modern shelter for this word.
normal.cn: 静音键是这个词在当代最日常的落脚处。

normal.en: Stay on mute in a meeting is the same idea as staying mute in a room.
normal.cn: 会议里「保持静音」和房间里「保持沉默」是同一个意思。

normal.en: Compare silent: silent is simply no sound, mute usually means speech is blocked or refused.
normal.cn: 对比 silent：silent 只是没有声音，mute 多指说话被拦住或被拒绝。

abstract.en: See a mouth open wide while the air stays perfectly still.
abstract.cn: 看着一张张大的嘴，空气却纹丝不动。

abstract.en: Picture a small speaker icon and a thin line drawn through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小喇叭图标上被画了一道细斜线。

abstract.en: Imagine a trumpet with a soft cloth stuffed in its bell.
abstract.cn: 想象小号的喇叭口里塞进了一块软布。

examples.en: She stayed mute about her reasons for leaving.
examples.cn: 她对自己离开的原因保持沉默。

examples.en: Please keep your microphone mute during the lecture.
examples.cn: 讲座期间请把麦克风保持静音。

examples.en: The bell sounded mute and distant in the fog.
examples.cn: 雾中钟声闷哑而遥远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「缪特」——像是把人「木」住、嘴封成一「特」别安静的木头人，就那么沉默着；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mutus（沉默的；不能说话的）→ 古法语 muet → 中古英语 mute → 现代英语 mute，核心义「嘴巴不出声」；再由「出声被压住」扩展到静音设备、弱音器、低沉的颜色与无声的见证。

sensesIntro.en: Mute begins with chosen silence, moves to the loss of speech, then to machines and sounds that have been quieted, then to muted colour, to the silencer itself, and finally to anything wordless.
sensesIntro.cn: mute 先指有意的沉默，再指失去说话能力，之后转到被调成安静的机器与声音，再到柔和的颜色、消音器物本身，最后落在一切无言之物上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mouth opens, but no sound comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴张开了，却没有一点声音出来。

branches.en: Deliberate silence is the first and most common sense.
branches.cn: 有意沉默是第一也是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Physical inability to speak is the original medical sense.
branches.cn: 生理上不能说话是最初的含义。

branches.en: Devices and controls that silence sound descend from the adjective.
branches.cn: 让声音消失的设备与按键由形容词延伸而来。

branches.en: Dulled sound and pale colour share the same lowered intensity.
branches.cn: 闷哑的声音与淡雅的颜色共享同样的强度降低。

branches.en: Chosen silence lets even objects become mute witnesses.
branches.cn: 有意的沉默让连物体都能成为无声的见证。

intro.en: Mute is a bare Latin stem, extended in English by -ly, -ness, and -ed, and shared with the sound words mutter and murmur.
intro.cn: mute 是一个不带前后缀的拉丁词干，在英语里靠 -ly、-ness、-ed 扩展，并与表示声音的 mutter、murmur 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutus is the base; the same closed-lip idea runs through muttire, to mutter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mutus 是词基；同一种闭唇发声的意思贯穿 muttire（嘟囔）。

items.example: Mutus is the direct Latin source of mute.
items.exampleCN: mutus 是 mute 的直接拉丁来源。

items.example: Muttire keeps the same closed-lip idea.
items.exampleCN: muttire 延续了同一种闭唇发声的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mutely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 mutely。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms muteness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 muteness。

items.meaningCN: 已经被变得……（构成形容词）
items.example: The ending -ed forms muted from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 由动词构成 muted。

items.example: Mute works as both adjective and verb.
items.exampleCN: mute 既可作形容词也可作动词。

items.example: Mutely describes silent action.
items.exampleCN: mutely 描述无声的动作。

items.example: Muteness names the state itself.
items.exampleCN: muteness 指这种状态本身。

items.example: Muted colours are soft colours.
items.exampleCN: muted colours 指柔和的颜色。

definition_zh: （船舰或军队中下属对长官的）哗变；叛变；兵变；哗变罪；发动哗变
definition_en: a rebellion against lawful authority by sailors or soldiers, chiefly on a ship, or to take part in such a rebellion
core_image: 船员在中舱低声密谋，推举出新的领头人，拒绝再听船长的命令
scene: 船在海上困了半个多月，补给见底，船长却仍不准返航。The crew withdrew their obedience and faced charges of mutiny.
sceneCN: 这里 mutiny 是「哗变、叛乱」（第 1 个义项：船员或士兵公开违抗上级）；句意为船员拒绝再服从命令，并因此被控哗变。船上还能看到裂开的帆布和空了的淡水池。

pos.zh: 名词：哗变、叛变、兵变；哗变罪
动词：哗变、叛乱、反抗长官

collocations.zh: 著名的邦蒂号事件式叛变

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表人后缀 -eer 构成，义为「哗变者、叛变者」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「哗变的、不服从的、难以驾驭的」
由形容词 mutinous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「倔强违抗地」

senses.title: An open revolt against a commanding officer
senses.definition: an open, organized refusal by sailors or soldiers to obey a lawful commanding officer
senses.definitionCN: 船员或士兵公开、有组织地拒绝服从合法指挥官
senses.example: The officers were taken prisoner in a night-time mutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 军官们在一场夜间的哗变中被扣押。
senses.why: The Latin source means a movement or an upheaval; a crew that moves as a body has risen against the man who orders it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「移动、动荡」；整条船的人一起动起来，就是背离下达命令的人。

senses.title: Rebellion in the army or on shore
senses.definition: a collective rebellion by soldiers or a group under authority, also used outside ships
senses.definitionCN: 士兵或受管辖的群体集体造反，这一用法也超出船舰范围
senses.example: The colonial troops staged a mutiny over unpaid wages.
senses.exampleCN: 殖民地军队因欠薪而发动叛乱。
senses.why: The ship sense loosens when the same refusal spreads on land; what stays constant is a group breaking off from its officer.
senses.whyCN: 当同样的拒绝在陆上蔓延开来，船上的那一义就放宽了；始终不变的是群体与长官脱钩。

senses.title: The legal offence of mutinying
senses.definition: the legal charge of unlawfully resisting or overthrowing the authority of a superior
senses.definitionCN: 非法抗拒或推翻上级权威的法律罪名
senses.example: He was sentenced for mutiny under naval law.
senses.exampleCN: 他根据海军法被以哗变罪判刑。
senses.why: Naval codes named the movement as a crime, so mutiny also denotes the charge laid against those who carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 海军法典把这场运动定为罪行，于是 mutiny 也指据此起诉当事人的罪名。

senses.title: To rebel against authority
senses.definition: to take part in or start a rebellion against a lawful commanding officer
senses.definitionCN: 参与或发动对合法指挥官的叛乱
senses.example: Two hundred sailors mutinied after months without shore leave.
senses.exampleCN: 两百名水手在数月无法上岸后发动了哗变。
senses.why: The verb is the noun put into action: the same rising now said as something people do.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词化为动作：同样的「起而反抗」现在被说成人们所做的事。

senses.title: A metaphor for refusing an order
senses.definition: a figurative revolting against any authority, as when children or workers turn against a leader
senses.definitionCN: 比喻式地反抗任何权威，如孩子或工人对抗领导者
senses.example: The editors declared a cheerful mutiny against the rule that banned humour.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑们轻松地对那条禁止幽默的规定来了场抗命。
senses.why: The battle-ship image is borrowed any time a group of people refuse to be steered by the one in charge.
senses.whyCN: 每当一群人拒绝被掌权者操控，战舰上的意象就被借用来形容。

intro.en: Mutiny reached English from French, which took it from Latin, and every stage keeps the idea of movement of a word.
intro.cn: mutiny 经法语进入英语，而法语又来自拉丁语，每一个阶段都保留了「话语」意义上的流动。

items.en: Latin movere means to move, push or set in motion; the deeper Indo-European origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 movere 意为「移动、推动、使动起来」；更早的印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: Post-classical Latin mutina names a movement, a riot or a state of disorder.
items.cn: 后古典时期拉丁语 mutina 指运动、骚乱或失序状态。

items.en: The verb mutiner means to rise up against authority and was used of soldiers; Old French spelling is reproduced as source uncertain.
items.cn: 法语动词 mutiner 意为反抗权威，多用于士兵；较早的古法语拼写形式属于来源不确定。

items.en: Mutiny enters English in the sixteenth century, at first mostly as a verb of soldiers rebelling against officers.
items.cn: mutiny 在十六世纪进入英语，最初多作动词，指士兵反抗军官。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the noun mutiny becomes the fixed word for a ship-borne revolt, and naval laws define it as a capital offence.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，名词 mutiny 成为指船舰上叛乱的固定说法，海军法规也把它定为重罪。

items.en: In modern use mutiny is loosened into metaphor for any group refusing a leader, while the strict ship sense remains in history and law.
items.cn: 现代英语中 mutiny 被放宽成任何群体拒绝领导的比喻，而严格意义上的船舰义仍保留在历史与法律文本里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word family built on mov-, and the near-meaning group gathers other words for rising against authority.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕 mov- 构成的词族；近义组收其他表示「起来反抗权威」的词。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in a mutiny.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「哗变者、叛变者」。

entries.definition: Rebellious, or showing a refusal to obey.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「哗变的、不服从的」。

entries.definition: To travel to work regularly, or to change one punishment for a lighter one; shares the Latin root move.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「通勤」或「减刑」，与 mutiny 共享拉丁语词根 movere「移动」。

entries.definition: Something whose form has changed through mutation; it looks related but comes from Latin mutare, only spelling similar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变体、突变体」；只是拼写相近，词源来自拉丁语 mutare「改变」，与 mutiny 的词源不同。

entries.definition: An organised attempt to fight against a government or ruler; broader and more political than mutiny.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叛乱、起义」，泛指对抗政府或统治者的有组织行动，比 mutiny 更宽、更具政治色彩。

entries.definition: A violent rising of people against those in power; formal in tone and often about a whole population.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴动、起义」，语气正式，多指民众整体的反抗。

entries.definition: A sudden and often violent taking of power, usually by a small group of insiders rather than soldiers in ranks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「政变」，指小圈子内部突然夺取权力，而不同于下级士兵的集体造反。

entries.definition: A refusal to work as a protest; related refusal of authority but in workplace rather than military form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「罢工」，同样是对权威的拒绝，但发生在工作场所而非军队。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work with the real root movere, the word family and the set phrases mutiny actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实词根 movere、同族词以及 mutiny 实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere means to move: a whole crew moves together against the officer in charge.
normal.cn: movere 是「移动」：整条船的人一起动起来，背离掌权者。

normal.en: A mutineer is a person who mutinies; the suffix -eer marks people such as musketeer and pamphleteer.
normal.cn: mutineer 是发动哗变的人，后缀 -eer 常用于指人，如 musketeer、pamphleteer。

normal.en: Mutinous is the adjective for the mood and for the sailor: a mutinous mood, a mutinous crew.
normal.cn: mutinous 是形容词，用来修饰气氛与人：a mutinous mood 是「叛逆的气氛」。

normal.en: Compare rebellion: rebellion is general and political, mutiny is specifically soldiers or sailors against their own officers.
normal.cn: 对比 rebellion：rebellion 泛指政治叛乱，mutiny 专指士兵或水手反抗自己的长官。

normal.en: The forms are simple: mutinies, mutinied, mutinying, changing y to i before a vowel ending.
normal.cn: 动词变化很规律：mutinies、mutinied、mutinying，在元音结尾前把 y 变成 i。

abstract.en: Picture a ship at dusk with the crew gathered in a circle, each holding a lamp, refusing the captain their respect.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏的船上，船员围成一圈，人各持一盏灯，不再向船长致敬。

abstract.en: Imagine an army camp where tents are struck before dawn, and the same refusal to obey spreads across the field.
abstract.cn: 想象军营在天亮前就拔营，同样的抗命在整片营地蔓延。

abstract.en: Picture someone writing the word mutiny on a charge sheet, turning the deed into a crime on paper.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把 mutiny 这个词写在起诉书里，把行为转成纸面上的罪名。

examples.en: The crew staged a mutiny after weeks without fresh water.
examples.cn: 船员在数周没有淡水之后发动了哗变。

examples.en: The captain feared that the men would mutiny before reaching port.
examples.cn: 船长担心船员在抵港前会哗变。

examples.en: History books describe several mutinies in the fleet that year.
examples.cn: 历史书记载了那一年舰队里发生的几场哗变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「谬提你」——荒谬地把你提起来另立新头，就是哗变；这只是谐音联想，并不代表词源。

root: 一般认为拉丁语 movere「移动」是更早的同源词根；后古典拉丁语 mutina 指骚乱、动乱，进入法语作 mutiner「造反」，再经英语作 mutiny「哗变」。更早的印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Mutiny moves from the concrete revolt on a ship, through the army and legal uses of the same act, to the verb that names it and finally to a loose metaphor for refusing any leader.
sensesIntro.cn: mutiny 从船舰上具体的哗变开始，经同样行为的军队与法律用法，到指称这一动作的动词，最后放宽为对任何领导的抗命比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crew that stops obeying its captain and moves as one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群船员不再服从船长，而是一起动起来。

branches.en: The ship sense is the concrete heart: officers held prisoner and the crew in command.
branches.cn: 船舰义是具体核心：军官被扣押，船员接管指挥。

branches.en: The army and shore sense widens the same refusal beyond the deck.
branches.cn: 军队与陆上义把同样的拒绝从甲板扩展到更多场合。

branches.en: Once naval law names the act, mutiny also means the offence charged in court.
branches.cn: 海军法规一旦为这一行为命名，mutiny 也就兼指法庭起诉的罪名。

branches.en: The verb packs the whole scene into a single act of rising.
branches.cn: 动词把整个场景压缩成一个「起而反抗」的动作。

branches.en: The metaphor lets ships leave the picture: any group refusing its leader now mutinies.
branches.cn: 比喻让船舰形象退到背景：任何拒绝领导的群体都可以「哗变」。

intro.en: Mutiny has no productive English prefix; its family is built by adding -eer to name people and -ous to name the mood.
intro.cn: mutiny 在现代英语里没有能产的词缀，其词族靠加 -eer 指人、加 -ous 表状态构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms behind mutiny are movere and the later mutina; the intermediate French stage is recorded for mutiner.
latinIntro.cn: 支撑 mutiny 的拉丁语形式是 movere 与较晚的 mutina；中间的法语阶段在 mutiner 上有文献记录。

items.meaningCN: 表状态或动作的名词词尾
items.example: The ending carries the noun from the French verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词从法语动词带了进来。

items.example: Mutiny names the revolt itself.
items.exampleCN: mutiny 指叛变这件事本身。

items.example: The suffix -eer forms mutineer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eer 构成 mutineer。

items.meaning: a person who takes part in a mutiny
items.example: A mutineer faces naval charges.
items.exampleCN: 哗变者会面临海军的指控。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous forms mutinous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 mutinous。

items.example: Mutinous describes the mood on deck.
items.exampleCN: mutinous 形容甲板上的人心状态。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mutinously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 mutinously。

items.example: The men answered mutinously.
items.exampleCN: 那些人以违抗的语气回答。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms mutinying.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 mutinying。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词
items.example: The suffix -ed forms mutinied.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 mutinied。

definition_zh: 天真的；幼稚的；朴实的；不谙世故的；（艺术风格）稚拙的
definition_en: lacking experience of the world, so trusting or simple in a way that may be charming or foolish; also used of art that avoids learned technique
core_image: 一个刚出生不久的人，看什么都新鲜，对谁都不设防
scene: 刚进城的年轻人第一次坐上地铁，把钱包借给热情搭话的陌生人。It was naive of him to trust a stranger with his wallet.
sceneCN: 这里 naive 是「天真的、轻信的」（第 1 个义项：因为缺少阅历而轻易相信别人）；句意为他把钱包交给陌生人，实在太天真了。地铁车厢里还有一只张着重重的广告灯箱。

pos.zh: 形容词：天真的；幼稚的；朴实的；不谙世故的；稚拙的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「天真、轻信」，英式也用 naivete 的不带符号拼法
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「天真地、轻率地」
由本词直接加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「天真」，较少使用

senses.title: Trusting because of inexperience
senses.definition: too trusting or simple, because one has not yet learned how the world really works
senses.definitionCN: 因为还没摸清世道而过分轻信或过于单纯
senses.example: She was naive enough to believe every promise made in the advertisement.
senses.exampleCN: 她天真到相信广告里的每一个承诺。
senses.why: The French source means inborn or native; a person still close to birth has not yet learned caution, so naivety is trust before experience.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「天生的、本性的」；一个仍然像刚出生的人还没学会防备，所以天真就是先于阅历的信任。

senses.title: Simple and free of tricks
senses.definition: simple, direct and without hidden motive, often used with mild affection
senses.definitionCN: 简单直接、没有隐藏动机，常带一点亲昵感
senses.example: There is something naive and charming about his honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 他的那份老实有着某种近乎天真的可爱。
senses.why: When the missing experience is not turned into a fault, the same simplicity is praised as plainness of heart.
senses.whyCN: 当那份缺少的阅历不当作缺点来看时，同样的单纯就被称赞为心地纯朴。

senses.title: Art avoiding learned rules
senses.definition: used of painting or writing that deliberately ignores academic technique and keeps a childlike directness
senses.definitionCN: 形容有意摆脱学院技法的绘画或写作，保留童稚般的直接
senses.example: The gallery shows naive paintings by village artists.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆展出乡村画家的稚拙派作品。
senses.why: In art criticism the word turns inborn simplicity into a style: an artist who never learned the formal rules of perspective is called naive.
senses.whyCN: 在艺术评论里，这个词把「天生的简朴」变成了风格：从未学过透视规则的画家就被称作稚拙派。

senses.title: A naive idea or plan
senses.definition: of an idea, plan or policy, based on an unrealistically simple picture of how people behave
senses.definitionCN: 形容想法、计划或政策，建立在对人和事过于简单的想象之上
senses.example: It was naive to think the reform would work without funding.
senses.exampleCN: 以为这项改革没有资金也能奏效，就太幼稚了。
senses.why: An idea can be as inexperienced as a person: it has not yet met the obstacles that a real street or budget would put in its way.
senses.whyCN: 想法也可以像人一样缺少阅历：它还没遇到过现实街道或预算会摆出的那些障碍。

intro.en: Naive is a borrowing from French, where it was the feminine form of an adjective meaning natural or inborn; the masculine naif still survives in older English spelling.
intro.cn: naive 是从法语借入的词形，来自法语形容词的阴性形式，原义为「天生的、自然的」；旧拼法 naif 是它的阳性形式。

items.en: Latin nativus means born, natural or innate, formed from nasci, to be born; the same root gives nature and native.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nativus 意为「天生的、自然的」，由 nasci「出生」构成；同一词根还生出 nature 与 native。

items.en: Old French keeps the adjective as naif, with the feminine naive, meaning natural or rustic.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个形容词 naif，阴性作 naive，意为「自然的、乡野的」。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the French adjective has acquired the sense of simple or artless, especially of people without much experience.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，法语形容词已带有「单纯、不做作」的意思，尤其用于阅历不多的人。

items.en: English borrows the word in both spellings, naif and naive; exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语同时借入 naif 与 naive 两种拼法；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The spelling naive takes over, and art critics begin to use it for painters who never learned academic technique.
items.cn: 拼法 naive 逐渐成为主流，艺术评论开始用它指从未学过学院技法的画家。

items.en: In current English naive is strongly negative when it implies a person ignores the real world, yet mildly positive when it suggests plainness.
items.cn: 当代英语里，若暗示人无视现实，naive 带有明显贬义；若指单纯朴实，则略带褒义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Latin root for born; the near-meaning group gathers trusting, unworldly and inexperienced words with different degrees and tones.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁语「出生」词根的词；近义组收表示轻信、不谙世故、缺乏经验的词，程度与语气各有不同。

entries.definition: Belonging to a person by birth, or growing naturally in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「出生地的、本地的、原产的」。

entries.definition: The inborn character of a thing or person, or the physical world.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「本性、天性」或「自然界」，词根同为「出生」。

entries.definition: Present from birth rather than learned; overlaps strongly with the literal sense of naive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「天生的、固有的」，与 naive 的字面义「天生的」高度重合。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being naive; also written naivete without the accent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天真、轻信」，也写作 naivete 并省略重音符号。

entries.definition: Easily deceived; sharper and more negative than naive, which can sometimes be affectionate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「易受骗的」，比 naive 更尖锐、更贬义，而 naive 有时带亲昵意味。

entries.definition: Free of guilt or of knowledge of evil; a moral or legal word rather than a word about experience.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无罪的、纯洁的」，偏向道德或法律意义，而不是讲阅历。

entries.definition: Too willing to believe things on little evidence; formal and clearly critical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「轻信的」，语气正式且明确带有批评。

entries.definition: Lacking knowledge of ordinary life and its practical matters, often in a soft, forgiving tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不谙世故的」，语气较温和，与 naive 的「轻信」义场相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work with the real Latin root for born, related words and the phrases naive actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「出生」词根、同源词以及 naive 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Nativus means born: a naive person is one whose views date from birth, not from experience.
normal.cn: nativus 意为「出生的」：naive 的人，其看法来自出生而非阅历。

normal.en: Native, nature and innate share the root: all are about what comes with birth.
normal.cn: native、nature 与 innate 同源，都与「与生俱来」有关。

normal.en: Naivety is the noun, and the older masculine spelling naif still appears in old books.
normal.cn: naivety 是名词，较旧的阳性拼法 naif 仍见于旧书。

normal.en: Compare gullible: gullible means easy to cheat, while naive means lacking experience in general.
normal.cn: 对比 gullible：gullible 指容易被骗，naive 更偏向泛指缺少经验。

normal.en: The standard pronunciation has no vowel between i and v: say na-ear-v with a long i sound.
normal.cn: 标准读音在 i 与 v 之间没有元音，读作「奈-伊芙」，i 发长音。

abstract.en: Picture a newborn with wide open eyes holding a coin out to an adult without a second thought.
abstract.cn: 想象一个刚出生不久、眼睛睁得很大的孩子，毫不犹豫地把硬币递给大人。

abstract.en: Think of a patch of wild flowers growing clean and untrained next to an over-trimmed garden.
abstract.cn: 想象一片野花在修剪过度的园子旁边自然而未经训练地生长。

abstract.en: Imagine a child painting a whole town in flat bright colours because nobody has taught the rules of light yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子用平涂的鲜亮颜色画下整座小镇，因为还没有人教过他光影的规则。

examples.en: Only a naive reader would take the advertisement at face value.
examples.cn: 只有天真的读者才会把广告当真。

examples.en: It was naive of the planners to ignore local traffic.
examples.cn: 规划者忽略本地交通状况，实在幼稚。

examples.en: The museum holds a collection of naive painting from the countryside.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆收藏了一批来自乡村的稚拙派绘画。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「乃依芙」——乃（是）依着别人说话的小妹，天真好骗；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 nativus「天生的、自然的」来自 nasci「出生」，同一词根生出 native 与 nature；古法语作 naif，阴性 naive，法语再把这个词形传给英语，核心义是「尚处于出生状态、未经世事」。

sensesIntro.en: Naive starts from birth-like trust, turns the same simplicity into a charm, and then widens to art without learned rules and to ideas that ignore how things really work.
sensesIntro.cn: naive 从「像刚出生般轻信」出发，把同样的单纯转为一种可爱，随后扩展到不受学院训练的绘画，以及无视现实的想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newborn looking at the world with no guard up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个刚出生的人毫无防备地看着世界。

branches.en: The trusting sense is the core defect: no experience means no caution.
branches.cn: 轻信义是核心的一面：没有阅历就意味着没有防备。

branches.en: The simple sense flips the same lack of tricks into a virtue.
branches.cn: 朴实义把同样「没有心机」翻成了优点。

branches.en: Art criticism takes the simplicity as a deliberate style.
branches.cn: 艺术评论把这份单纯当作一种刻意的风格。

branches.en: The idea sense applies the same lack of experience to plans and policies.
branches.cn: 想法义把同样的缺乏阅历用到计划与政策上。

branches.en: Both a naive person and a naive plan fail to imagine what the real world will do.
branches.cn: 天真的人和幼稚的计划，都没能想象现实会如何反弹。

intro.en: Naive is a whole French adjective borrowed intact; English builds its family with ordinary suffixes such as -ly, -ty and -ness.
intro.cn: naive 是整词借入的法语形容词，英语用 -ly、-ty、-ness 等普通后缀扩展出它的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms behind naive are nativus and the verb nasci; the French stage is recorded for naif and naive.
latinIntro.cn: 支撑 naive 的拉丁语形式是 nativus 与动词 nasci；法语阶段在 naif 与 naive 上有文献记录。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Nativus is the direct Latin form.
items.exampleCN: nativus 是直接的拉丁语形式。

items.example: Naif is the masculine form borrowed into English.
items.exampleCN: naif 是借入英语的阳性形式。

items.example: Naive is the standard modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: naive 是现代标准拼法。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms naively.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 naively。

items.example: The suffix -ty forms naivety.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ty 构成 naivety。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms naiveness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 naiveness。

items.example: Naively describes how an action is done.
items.exampleCN: naively 描述动作进行的方式。

items.example: Naivety names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: naivety 指这种特质本身。

definition_zh: 纳米（十亿分之一米）；长度单位 nm；用于描述芯片、分子等微小的尺度
definition_en: a unit of length equal to one billionth of a metre, used to measure atoms, molecules and the tiny features of computer chips
core_image: 一根头发被切成上万段，取其中一段的长度，那还只是几十纳米
scene: 实验室里，显微镜下的硅片被画成一张密密的街道图。Modern chips are built with features only a few nanometers wide.
sceneCN: 这里 nanometer 是「纳米」（第 1 个义项：长度单位，等于十亿分之一米）；句意为现代芯片的线路特征只有几纳米宽。硅片旁还摆着放大镜和一把量尺。

pos.zh: 名词：纳米（长度单位，等于十亿分之一米）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「纳米的、纳米级的」
本词的英式拼法，含义完全相同，复数写作 nanometres
由本词的前半 nano- 与 technology 合成，义为「纳米技术」

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.definition: a unit of length equal to one billionth of a metre, written nm
senses.definitionCN: 长度单位，等于十亿分之一米，符号写作 nm
senses.example: One nanometer is one millionth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 一纳米是一毫米的百万分之一。
senses.why: Nano- descends from Greek nanos, a dwarf, so a nanometer is literally a dwarf metre, a metre shrunk to one billionth of its size.
senses.whyCN: nano- 来自希腊语 nanos「侏儒」，所以 nanometer 字面上就是「侏儒米」，缩到十亿分之一米的尺。

senses.title: The scale of atoms and chips
senses.definition: the scale used to describe features of atoms, molecules, proteins and the transistors on computer chips
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述原子、分子、蛋白质以及芯片晶体管特征尺寸的尺度
senses.example: An atom is about a tenth of a nanometer across.
senses.exampleCN: 一个原子的直径约为十分之一纳米。
senses.why: Because a nanometer is near the size of a few atoms, the unit became the natural ruler for the invisible world of molecules and circuits.
senses.whyCN: 因为一纳米接近几个原子的大小，这个单位自然成了分子与电路这个看不见的世界的量尺。

senses.title: A short form in light wavelengths
senses.definition: a unit often used to state the wavelength of visible light and of laser light
senses.definitionCN: 常用于表示可见光与激光光波波长的单位
senses.example: Green light has a wavelength near five hundred nanometers.
senses.exampleCN: 绿光的波长接近五百纳米。
senses.why: Visible light falls between roughly four hundred and seven hundred nanometers, so scientists quote it in this unit instead of fractions of a metre.
senses.whyCN: 可见光约在四百到七百纳米之间，科学家便用这个单位来报数，而不用一米的小数。

senses.title: Nanometer as a marketing size
senses.definition: used in industry to describe the smallest feature a manufacturing process can produce, as in a seven-nanometer chip
senses.definitionCN: 工业上用来说明某种工艺能达到的最小特征尺寸，如「七纳米芯片」
senses.example: The new factory produces nanometers far below earlier generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家新工厂能做出比前几代小得多的纳米级尺寸。
senses.why: Because smaller transistors mean more speed for less power, the number of nanometers printed on a chip became a kind of headline.
senses.whyCN: 晶体管越小，速度越快、功耗越低，于是印在芯片上的纳米数字就成了一种宣传标题。

intro.en: Nanometer joins an ancient Greek word for a dwarf to an ordinary Latin unit, and the combination was made possible by the metric prefixes of the late eighteenth century.
intro.cn: nanometer 把古希腊语里表示「侏儒」的词与一个普通的拉丁语单位拼在一起，而这样的拼接要归功于十八世纪末的米制前缀。

items.en: Greek nanos or nannos means a dwarf, a little man; the deeper origin of the word is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 nanos 或 nannos 意为「侏儒、小人」；这个词更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin metrum means a measure, itself borrowed from Greek metron; it also gives metre and geometry.
items.cn: 拉丁语 metrum 意为「量度」，本身借自希腊语 metron，还生出 metre 与 geometry。

items.en: The metric system added prefixes such as micro and kilo; nano- as a billionth prefix is usually dated to the nineteenth century and is generally credited to scientific committees rather than one inventor.
items.cn: 米制系统加入了 micro、kilo 等前缀；nano- 作为十亿分之一的前缀一般认为出自十九世纪的科学委员会，而非某一位发明者。

items.en: Nanometre and nanometer are recorded from the early twentieth century, when physics and chemistry began to work on the scale of molecules.
items.cn: 英语 nanometre 与 nanometer 自二十世纪初有记录，当时物理与化学开始研究分子尺度。

items.en: Electronics and the emerging field of nanotechnology spread the word from laboratories into industry and ordinary news.
items.cn: 电子工业与新兴的纳米科学把这个词从实验室带进了工业与普通新闻。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers similar metric units that begin the same way or measure on the same ladder; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of naming very small lengths.
note.cn: 形近组收开头相同、或处在同一量级阶梯上的米制单位；近义组收其他表示极短长度的方法。

entries.definition: A billionth of a gram; same nano- prefix but a unit of mass.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纳克」，同样用 nano- 前缀，但计量的是质量而非长度。

entries.definition: A billionth of a second; same nano- prefix but a unit of time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纳秒」，同样用 nano- 前缀，但计量的是时间而非长度。

entries.definition: A millionth of a metre, one thousand times larger than a nanometer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微米」，是百万分之一米，比纳米大一千倍。

entries.definition: A thousandth of a metre, a million times larger than a nanometer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「毫米」，是千分之一米，比纳米大一百万倍。

entries.definition: An old name for the micrometer, one thousand nanometers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微米」的旧称，等于一千纳米。

entries.definition: A unit of length equal to a tenth of a nanometer, once common in atomic and molecular work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「埃」，等于十分之一纳米，曾广泛用于原子与分子测量。

entries.definition: The general name for the size range from one to a hundred nanometers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纳米尺度」，泛指一纳米到一百纳米之间的尺寸范围。

entries.definition: Smaller than one micrometer; a threshold term used in chip and particle work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「亚微米的」，在芯片与颗粒研究中常用作门槛标准。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek and Latin parts of the word, the metric ladder and the places a nanometer actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的希腊语与拉丁语构件、米制阶梯，以及纳米实际出现的场合。

normal.en: Nanos is Greek for dwarf: nanometer is a dwarf metre.
normal.cn: nanos 在希腊语里是「侏儒」：nanometer 就是「侏儒米」。

normal.en: Meter comes from Latin metrum, a measure from Greek metron, as in geometry, measuring the earth.
normal.cn: meter 来自拉丁语 metrum「量度」，源出希腊语 metron，如同 geometry 就是「量地」。

normal.en: Walk up the ladder: micro is a millionth, nano is a billionth, pico is a trillionth.
normal.cn: 沿阶梯往上看：micro 是百万分之一，nano 是十亿分之一，pico 是万亿分之一。

normal.en: The British writing nanometre keeps the same meaning, and both are abbreviated nm.
normal.cn: 英式写法 nanometre 含义相同，两种写法都缩写成 nm。

normal.en: Nanotechnology takes the nano- of nanometer and joins it to technology: work done at the size of a few nanometers.
normal.cn: nanotechnology 取 nanometer 的前缀 nano- 加上 technology：指在几纳米尺度上做的工作。

abstract.en: Picture one metre of rope cut into a billion equal pieces, then pick up a single one of them.
abstract.cn: 想象把一米长的绳子切成十亿段，然后拿起其中仅仅一段。

abstract.en: Place a few atoms side by side: the width across them is about one nanometer.
abstract.cn: 把几个原子并排摆开，横跨它们的宽度大约就是一纳米。

abstract.en: Picture a chip factory advertising a number so tiny it is printed next to the word nanometer.
abstract.cn: 想象一家芯片厂在做广告，数字小到必须写在 nanometer 这个词旁边。

examples.en: A human hair is about a hundred thousand nanometers thick.
examples.cn: 一根头发的粗细约为十万纳米。

examples.en: The engineers reduced the gap between the wires to ten nanometers.
examples.cn: 工程师把导线之间的间隙缩小到了十纳米。

examples.en: In nanometer scale, the surface of the material behaves quite differently.
examples.cn: 在纳米尺度下，这种材料的表面表现大不相同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「难没米」——再小的地方竟然连一粒米都塞不进去，所以是极小的长度单位；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 希腊语 nanos「侏儒、小人」+ 拉丁语 metrum「量度」，中间借米制前缀 nano-「十亿分之一」，合起来指「十亿分之一米的长度」，核心义是「侏儒般微小的量尺」。

sensesIntro.en: Nanometer is first a plain unit of length, then the scale of atoms and chips, then a common way to quote light wavelengths, and finally a figure used to advertise how small a process can go.
sensesIntro.cn: nanometer 首先是单纯的长度单位，接着是原子与芯片的尺度、光波长的常用表示，最后成为宣传工艺精细程度的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metre stick shrunk to the size of a dwarf, so small that a few atoms would fill it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根米尺缩成侏儒般的个头，小到几个原子就能填满。

branches.en: The unit sense is the literal meaning: a billionth of a metre.
branches.cn: 单位义是字面含义：十亿分之一米。

branches.en: The atomic sense puts the unit to work where atoms and transistors are measured.
branches.cn: 原子义把这个单位用在原子与晶体管的测量上。

branches.en: The light sense uses the unit for wavelengths of visible and laser light.
branches.cn: 光的义项用这个单位来表示可见光与激光的波长。

branches.en: The industry sense turns the number into a claim about how small a factory can build.
branches.cn: 工业义把数字变成对工厂能造多小的宣称。

branches.en: The plain unit and the atomic scale are the same length seen from two viewpoints.
branches.cn: 单纯单位义与原子尺度义，是同一长度从两个角度看。

intro.en: Nanometer is a compound of a Greek prefix and a Latin unit; the family grows with nano- before other words.
intro.cn: nanometer 是由希腊语前缀与拉丁语单位合成的词；同族词则由 nano- 加在其他词前面形成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin part is metrum, a measure; the nano- part comes from Greek nanos, a dwarf, and both are recorded forms rather than reconstructions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语部分是 metrum「量度」；nano- 部分来自希腊语 nanos「侏儒」，两者都是有文献记录的形式，而非重构形式。

items.example: The prefix nano- marks the tiny scale.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 nano- 标出极小的尺度。

items.example: Nanos gives the idea of smallness.
items.exampleCN: nanos 提供「小」的意念。

items.example: Metrum is the Latin form of the unit.
items.exampleCN: metrum 是这个单位的拉丁语形式。

items.example: Nanometer joins the prefix and the unit.
items.exampleCN: nanometer 把前缀与单位合在一起。

items.example: The combining form -meter also appears in thermometer.
items.exampleCN: 组合成分 -meter 也见于 thermometer。

items.example: American writers prefer the nanometer spelling.
items.exampleCN: 美式写法偏好 nanometer 这种拼法。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms nanometric.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 nanometric。

items.example: Nanometric describes structures of this size.
items.exampleCN: nanometric 形容这个尺寸的结构。

items.meaningCN: 构词用前缀，见于纳米技术类词语
items.example: Nano- also begins nanotechnology and nanoscale.
items.exampleCN: nano- 也用于 nanotechnology 与 nanoscale 等词的开头。

items.example: The abbreviation nm is written after a number.
items.exampleCN: 缩写 nm 写在数字之后。

definition_zh: 麻醉药；镇静剂；毒品；麻醉的；催眠的
definition_en: a drug that dulls pain and makes the senses numb, usually a strong painkiller or an illegal drug
core_image: 一杯让人整条手臂发麻的苦药，痛觉被关掉了
scene: 深夜的急诊室里，值班医生要给摔断腿的病人打一针强效止痛剂，让剧痛暂时消失，好让手术顺利进行。The doctor gave the patient a narcotic so that the terrible pain of the broken leg faded before the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 narcotic 是「麻醉药、强效止痛剂」（第 1 个义项：使疼痛与知觉麻木的药物）；句意：医生给病人用了一剂麻醉药，让断腿的剧痛在手术前消退。

pos.zh: 麻醉药；镇静剂；烈性毒品

derivatives.zh: 由 narcotic 加 -al- 与副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以麻醉的方式」
同一希腊词根，表示由药物或麻醉气体造成的「麻木状态、麻醉」
希腊语 narkē（麻木）加 lepsis（发作、抓住），义为「发作性睡病」
源于希腊语 narkē 的构词成分，多用于毒品与麻醉相关的新词

senses.title: A painkilling drug
senses.definition: a drug, usually one containing an opioid, that dulls pain and brings sleep or numbness
senses.definitionCN: 通常含鸦片类成分、能减轻疼痛并使人昏睡或麻木的药物
senses.example: The doctor gave the patient a narcotic to control the pain.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给病人用了一剂麻醉药来控制疼痛。
senses.why: Greek narkē means numbness, so the word names a drug whose whole action is to switch off feeling.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 narkē 意为「麻木」，所以这个词直接指向一种把感觉关掉的药：它的全部作用就是让人不再觉得痛。

senses.title: The adjective of numbing
senses.definition: of or relating to such a drug, or having the power to numb and send people to sleep
senses.definitionCN: 与这类药物有关的，或具有使人麻木、使人入睡作用的
senses.example: The herb has a mild narcotic effect on a nervous patient.
senses.exampleCN: 这种草药对紧张的病人有轻微的麻醉作用。
senses.why: The same Greek root yields the adjective, because the quality of the drug and the drug itself were one idea: numbness.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词根顺理成章地长出形容词，因为药物的性质与药物本身在古人的观念里是一件事：麻木。

senses.title: An illegal drug
senses.definition: an illegal, habit forming drug such as opium, heroin or cocaine
senses.definitionCN: 鸦片、海洛因、可卡因等非法且易成瘾的毒品
senses.example: Customs officers found a bag of narcotics hidden in the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 海关人员在卡车里发现了一包藏匿的毒品。
senses.why: Modern law kept the Greek numbness but narrowed it: the numbing drug that is banned and traded illegally is called a narcotic.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律保留了「麻木」的核心，却把范围收窄：被禁止、被非法交易的那种麻木类药物就叫 narcotic。

senses.title: Anything that soothes
senses.titleCN: 麻醉品似的东西；使人麻木的东西
senses.definition: anything that dulls awareness or keeps a person from facing reality
senses.definitionCN: 任何使人意识迟钝、回避现实的东西
senses.example: Cheap entertainment can act as a narcotic for a tired mind.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的娱乐对疲惫的心灵来说就像一剂麻醉药。
senses.why: Anything that switches off feeling can borrow the name, so the word extends from chemistry to habit and comfort.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能把感觉关掉的东西都能借用这个词，于是它的用法从化学一路延伸到习惯与安慰。

intro.en: Narcotic comes from Greek narkōtikos, meaning numbing, from narkē, numbness.
intro.cn: narcotic 来自希腊语 narkōtikos（使麻木的），源于希腊语 narkē（麻木）。

items.en: Narkē means numbness or a benumbed state.
items.cn: 希腊语 narkē 意为「麻木」或「麻木的状态」。

items.en: The verb narkan means to benumb, and narkōtikos describes what numbs.
items.cn: 动词 narkan 意为使麻木，narkōtikos 则形容能使人麻木的事物。

items.en: Medieval Latin takes the Greek adjective as narcoticus.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语借用这个希腊形容词，写作 narcoticus。

items.en: Latin and French forms bring the word close to English, though the earliest dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语与法语的形式把词带入英语，但最早出现年代存在不确定。

items.en: Narcotic names a drug that dulls the senses and deadens pain.
items.cn: 英语中 narcotic 指使感官麻木、减轻疼痛的药物。

items.en: Law narrows the word to habit forming and illegal drugs.
items.cn: 法律把该词收窄为易成瘾的非法毒品。

note.en: Narcotic belongs to the Greek numbness family and sits near the ordinary words for drugs and sleep.
note.cn: narcotic 属于希腊语「麻木」词族，并与表示药物与睡眠的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: Greek word for numbness
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语「麻木」；此处只借用希腊词形说明词根，英语中并不单用

entries.definition: a state of numbness or stupor caused by drugs
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词：药物或麻醉气体造成的麻木、昏睡状态

entries.definition: a disorder that causes sudden sleep attacks
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词：发作性睡病，病人会突然入睡

entries.definition: a drug that calms and makes people sleepy
entries.definitionCN: 镇静药：使人平静、昏睡，但不主打止痛

entries.definition: a drug derived from opium, or something that dulls feeling
entries.definitionCN: 鸦片制剂：由鸦片提取，属于 narcotic 的一类

entries.definition: any substance taken to affect the body or mind
entries.definitionCN: 药物；毒品：上位词，涵盖合法的药物与非法的毒品

normalIntro.en: Narcotic is built on Greek narkē, numbness, and the whole word family in English repeats that numbness.
normalIntro.cn: narcotic 建立在希腊语 narkē（麻木）之上，英语中这一整族词都在重复「麻木」这件事。

normal.en: The root nark- means numb, so a narcotic is literally a numbing thing.
normal.cn: 词根 nark- 意为麻木，所以 narcotic 字面上就是「使人麻木的东西」。

normal.en: Narcosis is the stony numbness the drug produces, and narcolepsy is a sleep attack.
normal.cn: 同根词 narcosis 是药物造成的麻木状态，narcolepsy 则是突然发作的睡眠。

normal.en: Narcotic drugs are strong painkillers, and the plural narcotics often means illegal drugs.
normal.cn: 搭配 narcotic drugs 指强效止痛药，复数 narcotics 则常指毒品。

normal.en: Narcotic effect means the way the drug dulls the senses.
normal.cn: narcotic effect 指的是药物让感官变迟钝的作用。

normal.en: Narcotic may sit on a label beside a warning that it can cause dependence.
normal.cn: narcotic 常出现在药品标签上，旁边往往写着可能导致依赖的警告。

abstract.en: Picture an arm going heavy and warm, like a limb asleep after a long squeeze.
abstract.cn: 想象一条手臂变得又沉又暖，像被人长时间压过之后发麻失去知觉。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp dimmed by a hand: bright pain fades to a soft grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把灯调暗：尖锐的疼痛慢慢褪成柔和的灰色。

abstract.en: See a bottle sealed with a warning label, sold only to people who carry permission.
abstract.cn: 想象一只贴着警告标签的瓶子，只卖给拿着许可的人。

examples.en: The hospital keeps strong narcotics in a locked cabinet.
examples.cn: 医院把强效麻醉药品锁在专门的柜子里。

examples.en: Trafficking in narcotics carries a heavy prison sentence.
examples.cn: 贩运毒品会被判处重刑。

examples.en: Some cold remedies have a narcotic effect that makes drivers drowsy.
examples.cn: 有些感冒药具有麻醉作用，会让司机昏昏欲睡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那儿可疼了」——把 narcotic 读成「那儿可疼」，所以要用它来止痛；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语词源无关。

root: 希腊语 narkē（麻木）+ narkan（使麻木）→ 希腊语 narkōtikos（使麻木的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 narcoticus → 英语 narcotic，核心义始终是「把感觉关掉」。同族还有 narcosis（麻醉状态）与 narcolepsy（发作性睡病）。

sensesIntro.en: Narcotic starts with the numbing drug itself, then its adjective sense, then the illegal drug of modern law, and finally anything that dulls the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: narcotic 先从使人麻木的药物本义出发，引申出形容词义，再被现代法律收窄为毒品，最后泛指一切使人麻木的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bitter draught that puts a whole arm to sleep.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯让整条手臂发麻的苦药。

branches.en: The concrete drug is the meaning of the noun.
branches.cn: 具体的药物是名词的本义。

branches.en: The medical quality of the drug becomes an adjective.
branches.cn: 药物的性质被抽象成形容词义。

branches.en: Law and crime narrow the word to banned substances.
branches.cn: 法律与犯罪语境把词收窄到被禁物质。

branches.en: A pharmacy stock and a street seizure use the same name for the same chemistry.
branches.cn: 药房里的存货和街头缴获的赃物，用同一个词指同一种化学作用。

branches.en: Both the drug and a tired habit can switch off feeling.
branches.cn: 药物与疲惫的习惯都能把感觉关掉。

intro.en: Narcotic is a Greek-derived word: the root nark- carries numbness, and the endings -otic and -osis build its family.
intro.cn: narcotic 是源自希腊语的词：词根 nark- 承载「麻木」，词尾 -otic 与 -osis 构成它的整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin adopted the Greek adjective as narcoticus, and Greek narkē stayed in scientific compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借用希腊形容词写成 narcoticus，希腊语 narkē 也一直保留在科学复合词里。

items.example: Narke is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: narkē 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Narkan gives the idea of putting feeling to sleep.
items.exampleCN: narkan 给出「让感觉入睡」的意象。

items.example: Narkotikos is the direct model of the English word.
items.exampleCN: narkōtikos 是英语词的直接原型。

items.example: The adjective keeps the Greek quality sense.
items.exampleCN: 形容词义保留了希腊语的性质义。

items.example: The noun points to the substance itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词义指向物质本身。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns the Greek root into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把希腊词根变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -osis forms narcosis.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -osis 构成 narcosis。

items.example: Narcosis names the state, not the drug.
items.exampleCN: narcosis 指状态而不是药物。

items.example: The suffix -lepsy forms narcolepsy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -lepsy 构成 narcolepsy。

items.example: The combining form builds new words about the drug trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个构词成分用来构成毒品交易相关的新词。
